prompts: We want a 3D scene someone would keep as a wallpaper: the classic view of Mount Fuji at dusk, with the red five-tier Chureito pagoda and cherry trees in bloom, in a low poly look with some gentle motion. Deliver it as {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code and no external models or textures. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
Scene renders. First revision: too dark, snow cap missing, pagoda top cropped, and a ridge silhouette cuts oddly across the right. Fixing lighting, snow line, and framing.

Good composition. Final round: clean up Fuji's snow cap (stray bright mid-slope facets) and lighten trunks.

The scene is complete and verified. Final state:

**[goal]** Single-file low-poly 3D wallpaper: Fuji at dusk, red five-tier Chureito pagoda, cherry trees, gentle motion.

**[action]** Built `scene/index.html` — one file, Three.js r170 via the allowed jsDelivr URL (importmap), Zen Old Mincho via Google Fonts, all geometry, materials and the sky shader generated in code; no models or textures. Delivered, then ran two live-browser revision rounds: brightened dusk lighting, fixed framing so the whole pagoda fits, and cleaned Fuji's jagged snow line.

**[result]** Verified by loading the actual file in a browser and screenshotting three times. The final render shows: gradient dusk dome (indigo → rose → warm horizon) with a sun glow behind the ridge, faceted Fuji with a snow cap, the vermilion five-tier pagoda with white walls, gold finial and stone terrace on the right, pink icosahedron-canopy cherry trees framing the view, drifting clouds, rocks, and petals in the air. Motion is real, not implied: between successive screenshots the petal field and camera position visibly shift (slow sinusoidal camera drift, 240 instanced falling petals, canopy sway, cloud drift). The caption renders in the loaded webfont, confirming both allowed network origins work.

**Assumptions stated:** dusk palette read as warm horizon under deepening indigo; "classic view" as pagoda-right / Fuji-centered composition with cherry trees in the mid ground; stylized low-poly (flat shading, 4-sided pagoda roofs) rather than exact architectural replication; gentle motion kept to camera sway, petals, canopies and clouds so it stays wallpaper-calm.

**How I know it is right:** the file opened with no build step in a browser restricted to the two allowed hosts, rendered without errors across three reloads, and each screenshot matches the brief's checklist items — Fuji, snow cap, five visible pagoda tiers, red color, blossoms, dusk light, and frame-to-frame differences proving the animation loop runs.
